title: Hawkins and Monk's tunes; first bop recordings
summary: Hawkins was crazy about Monk, and the date he organizes yields among the first bop records.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: But anyway these guys used to come around and hustle up different groups to make records, and at that time they had hustled Hawk up to make this record. Hawk wanted to be associated -- he was crazy about Thelonious Monk, and to my recollection Monk had the first modern tunes alive. I mean, if
you wanted to play any modern music you played Monk's tune. That was before Dizzy.
Yeah. But any way Hawk got us all together to make this record, and it of course was one of the first bop recordings, you know, and --
You don't remember the tune, do you?
The one that I wrote was called De Dakt But

That was in the bop language, you know, (Singing of tunes), you know. Dizzy wrote Woody 'Ya' Wouldn't You (Singing of Notes), a beautiful number, right today I don't think there's no better writing than that.
